daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The MPR and Constitutional Court signed an MoU covering constitutional interpretation and court rulings, with MPR leadership meeting the Court to discuss the constitutional amendment discourse. MPR Deputy Secretary-General Ahmad Muzani requested the Court hear MPR views before interpreting the constitution, signaling renewed tensions over institutional boundaries and the potential for constitutional reform.

  • Demokrat chairman AHY will conduct a safari to meet party leaders ahead of Demokrat's anniversary, while asserting that parties are now more mature and respect each other's political roles.
  • Detik.com reported that parties are "hunting Jokowi's blessing" within the Demokrat party (nicknamed "the elephant party").
  • Demokrat urged the DPR to expedite discussion of the electoral bill to allow sufficient time for public socialization, while Commission II has already drafted 28 DIM for the election law despite the working committee not yet being formed.
  • Former PKS politician Narji officially switched to PSI during a mass circumcision event, prompting a response from PKS following the defection.
  • MPR Chairman stated that Indonesia's delegation will invite ulama to attend Khamenei's funeral in Iran, though Tempo reported controversy surrounding the MPR chairman's appointment by Prabowo for this mission.
  • MPR Deputy Speaker Fadli Zon clarified that a new building at the palace is being constructed due to space shortages and insisted it will not be built on heritage sites.
  • The KPK is investigating a former MPR Secretary-General for allegedly demanding 10 percent fees from private parties in procurement contracts.

Foreign Policy & Defence

President Prabowo bid farewell to PM Modi as his state visit to India concluded, with the two countries signing 15 cooperation agreements covering nuclear energy technology exchange and other sectors. Prabowo expressed his admiration for Modi and presented an angklung as a ceremonial gift to the Indian Prime Minister. Modi promised that Indian tourist numbers to Prambanan would multiply, while India also pledged to increase affordable medicine supplies to Indonesia.

  • Following his meeting with Modi, Prabowo met former Thai PM Thaksin Shinawatra and his daughter at the Kertanegara residence in Jakarta.
  • Indonesia and Canada are exploring stronger infrastructure cooperation to deepen bilateral ties.
  • A high-level Indonesian delegation will depart Thursday for the funeral of Iran's Supreme Leader Khamenei.
  • The Indonesian Marine Corps demonstrated its readiness at the RIMPAC 2026 multinational naval exercise.
  • Finance Minister Purbaya commented on the budget for procuring India's BrahMos missiles.

Other

Police seized 74 kg of gold and Rp 282.4 billion in cash linked to three corruption cases, conducting raids at 13 locations including Café de'Clan, where they confiscated Rp 67 billion and stacks of US and Singapore dollars from safes. Officers also raided a house in Sentul, Bogor, seizing hundreds of kilograms of gold and suitcases filled with foreign currency in what represents one of the largest corruption-related asset seizures in recent years.

  • Finance Minister Purbaya gave a terse response regarding the US dollar pushing the rupiah to Rp 18,000, while the Indonesia Stock Exchange pledged to defend the country's emerging market status amid downgrade risks.
  • Indonesia and China's mRNA dengue vaccine will boost global health, according to BPOM, while the government launched a grant scheme to advance research and development of 11 vaccine antigens, with BRIN stating that vaccine development is key to health sovereignty.
  • Indonesia advanced its space program with the launch of the NEO-1 satellite.
  • Former British PM Tony Blair's visit signals global confidence in the Danantara sovereign wealth fund, while Indonesia's PFII initiative could attract up to US$27.7 billion in investment.
  • The Ministry of Religious Affairs proposed that hajj costs for 2027 increase to Rp 107 million, while the ministry also proposed redefining Islamic education and will strengthen health screening to monitor pilgrims from pre-departure.
